subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU selection, TPS targets & quantization tradeoffs
messages:
From: Samuel Park <samuel.park@quantifai.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@quantifai.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU selection, TPS targets & quantization tradeoffs

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align on sizing: 

Summary of QuantifAI workload (as discussed)
- Peak API TPS: ~180 requests/sec for scoring endpoint (p95 bursts up to ~270 TPS during business hours)
- Typical request profile: prompt ~120 tokens, expected completion ~900 tokens (autonomous summarization pipeline)
- Concurrency requirement: we need consistent p99 latency under 400ms for the interactive portion (shorter prompts) and can tolerate 800ms p99 for background batch completes.
- SLO objective: 99.5% availability and predictable tail latency — downtime impacts customer SLAs.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) GPU flavor guidance — you mentioned H100 vs A100 and a smaller L4 option for hosted fallback. For sustained throughput with this token mix, which do you recommend as primary for Dedicated?
2) Quantization — we can accept small quality delta for a 30-40% unit-cost reduction. What are your recommendations on int8 vs 4-bit quantization for our model family (LLaMA-3 style) on Dedicated?
3) Batching & cache — curious how much headroom we get from prefix/KV caching given many repeated prompts in our stream.

Attaching a short token-profile CSV (attached) to help with the sizing exercise. We can share sample traces if helpful.

Samuel
Ops Lead, QuantifAI

Attachments: quantifai_token_profile.csv (text/csv, 2.1 KB)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@quantifai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 18:24:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU selection, TPS targets & quantization tradeoffs

Thanks Samuel — good notes and appreciated the token profile. Short answers up front, then next steps: 

Short recommendations
- Primary GPU: A100-80GB for predictable p99 latency at your token mix; H100 provides better throughput for very large batch jobs but at a higher unit-cost and with less maturity on some quantized kernels today.
- Quantization: start with dynamic int8 for Dedicated evaluation (best tradeoff for LLaMA-3-style models). Move to 4-bit (Q4) only after targeted evals — we can run a small QA sweep.
- Caching/batching: prefix+KV caching expected to reduce billed tokens by ~15–25% on your repeated prompt patterns; autoscaling with conservative burst headroom (30%) recommended.

Notes and caveats
- Given your ~900-token completions, consider splitting interactive short-path traffic (low-latency) onto a smaller pool sized for latency (A100) and bulk long-completions onto a separate pool (H100 or quantized A100) to optimize cost. This is a hybrid Dedicated setup (two pools) rather than single monolithic pool.
- If you want strict p99 <= 400ms across all requests, you'll need higher concurrency buffer and more aggressive instance count — otherwise accept a latency tiering approach (fast path vs batch path).

Next steps
1) Karthik and Vivek — can you take the attached CSV and run the capacity calculator (see link) and produce a 2-option estimate: latency-optimized and cost-optimized?
2) Samuel — can you send a 10-minute sample trace (raw HTTP logs) or a small replay so we have real arrival patterns?

I'll loop back with a short two-slide decision matrix once we have the calc.

Best,
Maya
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Related link: https://redwood.app/s/drive/quantifai-capacity-brief-v2

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:11:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU selection, TPS targets & quantization tradeoffs

Looping in some math — I started a quick calc and posting assumptions here so Maya/Sam can vet: 

Assumptions (baseline)
- Model perf on A100-80GB: ~1.8 token/ms at 1k-token sequences (estimate from bench).
- H100: ~2.2 token/ms but 25% higher hourly cost in our preferred cloud SKU.
- Int8 quantization yields ~1.6x throughput improvement vs fp16 on A100; Q4 gives ~2.6x but with more variability on tail latency.

Preliminary sizing (round numbers)
- Latency-optimized pool (A100): target sustained 200 TPS with p99 headroom -> ~6 x A100-80GB (with 30% burst headroom)
- Cost-optimized split (A100 quantized + H100 for bulk): 3 x A100 (int8) + 2 x H100 for large completion bursts

Open items for accurate calc
- Exact token distribution (we need percent of requests under 200 tokens vs >600 tokens) — the attached CSV has bulk numbers but not percentile split.
- Arrival process: Poisson vs bursty pattern will change batching gains significantly.

I'll produce an XLS with the two-option worksheet and break out expected monthly unit cost. Will attach by EOD.

-Karthik
Principal Performance Eng | Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: redwood_capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 14 KB)

From: Samuel Park <samuel.park@quantifai.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU selection, TPS targets & quantization tradeoffs

Thanks — this is super helpful. A couple quick answers and confirmation: 

- Token percentiles: about 55% are under 200 tokens, ~30% fall between 200–600 tokens, and ~15% are long-form (>600 tokens). I'll attach a small trace I exported for the replay.
- We'll be comfortable starting with int8 and running a short A/B evaluation for Q4 on a canary pool. If quality delta is >2% on our automated scoring, we hold on Q4.
- Replay file attached (sanitized): quantifai_replay_05027.json (2.8 MB). Please let me know if you need raw logs instead.

Next: If Karthik posts the XLS, we'll pick the latency vs cost option and sign a 3-month commit for Dedicated pilot.

Cheers,
Samuel
Ops Lead, QuantifAI

Attachment: quantifai_replay_05027.json (application/json, 2.8 MB)
